reference.source: WHO Classification of Head and Neck Tumours
clinicalPearls: A rare benign tumour composed almost entirely of oncocytes: large cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm packed with mitochondria.
It most often affects the parotid in older adults and presents as a well-circumscribed, encapsulated, painless mass.
Unlike Warthin tumour, the classic oncocytoma lacks a lymphoid stroma, which is the key distinguishing histological feature.
Like Warthin tumour, oncocytes are avid for technetium pertechnetate, so scintigraphy is not discriminating between the two.
Diffuse or multifocal oncocytosis of the gland may coexist and can make complete separation of tumour from background difficult.
A clear-cell variant, due to intracytoplasmic glycogen, can mimic metastatic clear-cell renal carcinoma and warrants careful exclusion.
Immunohistochemistry with antimitochondrial antibody highlights the oncocytic cytoplasm and supports the diagnosis.
The principal diagnostic task is to distinguish it from oncocytic carcinoma, which shows infiltration, necrosis and increased mitoses.
reference.pathophysiology: Salivary gland oncocytoma results from clonal proliferation of oncocytes, epithelial cells that accumulate vast numbers of morphologically and often functionally abnormal mitochondria. The oncocytic phenotype reflects a compensatory mitochondrial hyperplasia thought to relate to acquired defects in mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, and its frequency increases with age; a history of prior irradiation is recognised in some cases. The tumour forms an encapsulated nodule of solid or organoid nests and cords of oncocytes with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and round nuclei. Because oncocytic metaplasia is common in ageing salivary tissue, oncocytoma exists on a continuum with focal and diffuse oncocytosis, and the abundant mitochondria account for both the tinctorial appearance and the radionuclide avidity.
additionalDifferentials: Metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (clear-cell variant)
additionalInvestigations: Technetium pertechnetate scintigraphy (uptake is supportive but non-specific)
MRI or CT to define extent
Exclusion of metastatic renal cell carcinoma when clear-cell morphology is present
redFlags: Infiltrative margins or tumour necrosis suggesting oncocytic carcinoma
Fixation to skin or deep tissues
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is excellent, as the tumour is benign and complete excision is curative. The main clinical importance lies in reliably distinguishing it from oncocytic carcinoma and from metastatic renal carcinoma.
pitfalls: Confusing oncocytoma with Warthin tumour or oncocytic carcinoma on limited material
Mistaking the clear-cell variant for metastatic renal cell carcinoma
Sampling background oncocytic metaplasia rather than the lesion itself
Relying on technetium avidity to distinguish it from Warthin tumour
